facts.detail: Ofcom published the Spring 2026 Connected Nations update on 13 May 2026.
The report provides a snapshot of fixed broadband and mobile coverage as of January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of homes.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 27.1 million homes, equal to 89%.
Ofcom estimated that about 4,000 premises lacked access to affordable decent broadband.

guard_streams.source: Mobile connectivity you can count on

facts.detail: Ofcom published the mobile-connectivity discussion paper on 3 June 2026.
The paper sets out what good mobile connectivity should look like and where current provision falls short.
Ofcom states that improvement requires action from industry, government, local authorities, landlords and other stakeholders.
Responses to the discussion paper are requested by 5pm on 29 July 2026.
Ofcom plans an update in early 2027 on lessons learned and next priorities.

guard_streams.source: Signal struggles on trains widespread, Ofcom research finds

facts.detail: Ofcom published the train-connectivity research findings on 3 June 2026.
The research measured mobile performance across 24 segments of key railway lines in England, Scotland and Wales.
Good performance was defined as at least 5 Mbit/s download, 1.5 Mbit/s upload and latency no higher than 50 ms.
The reported good-performance rates were EE 42%, Three 21%, O2 20% and Vodafone 17%.
On-board train Wi-Fi met the good-performance standard in only 1% of measurements.

facts.detail: The checker accepts a postcode to show local mobile coverage and broadband availability.
Mobile results are displayed by provider.
Broadband results include standard, superfast and ultrafast service availability.
Results can also be viewed through interactive maps.
Ofcom provides fixed and mobile coverage data through an API, but the checker does not report local maintenance or faults.

guard_streams.source: Your right to request a decent broadband service: What you need to know

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the broadband universal-service guidance on 20 March 2026.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Eligible premises can request an upgraded connection from BT, or KCOM in the Hull area.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and the estimated connection cost.
Network work costing £3,400 or less is covered, and the service price is capped at £59.60 per month.
